props.gloss_en: the mishna: R' Shimon exempts one who plucks from a pot, perforated or not
apparently, R' Shimon treats a perforated pot as an unperforated one
the baraita, R' Shimon: there is no difference between a perforated and an unperforated pot except for rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity]
for all matters R' Shimon treats [a perforated pot] as detached
impurity is different, for the Torah amplified purity for seeds, as it says 'upon any sowing seed that is sown' (Lev 11:37)
R' Zeira: R' Shimon agrees [to liability] if [the pot] was perforated to the measure of its purification
R' Shimon agrees [to liability] if [the pot] was perforated below a quarter-log
Rava: perforated [enough] to let liquid out -- pure from impurity as a shard, yet still a vessel for sanctifying the purification water
perforated to let liquid in -- unfit for sanctifying the purification water, yet still a vessel for rendering seeds in it susceptible
perforated like a small root -- no longer renders seeds susceptible, yet still a vessel for holding olives
perforated to let olives out -- pure as a vessel for holding olives, yet still a vessel for holding pomegranates
perforated to let pomegranates out -- pure from everything
and if it is surrounded by a sealed cover -- [it is not pure] until most of it is broken
Rav Asi: I heard -- the measure of an earthenware vessel is [a hole] letting out a pomegranate
Rava: perhaps you heard it only of a vessel surrounded by a sealed cover

and they said 'letting liquid out' only with regard to a shard

and one said: [the measure of an earthenware vessel is a hole] like a small root
R' Eliezer: the measure of an earthenware vessel is [a hole] letting out olives
and [such perforated vessels] are like dung, stone and earth vessels, which receive impurity neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic law
